newsitem.title: DUBAI: Top U.S. military official holds talks in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. military official holds talks in Saudi.

text.p: The chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, Army General John Shalikashvili, met Saudi Arabia's defence minister on Tuesday and discussed bilateral relations, the official Saudi Press Agency said.
The meeting with Saudi Defence and Aviation Minister Prince Sultan was also attended by senior U.S. diplomats and officers of the Saudi armed forces.
The agency did not say when Shalikashvili had arrived or give further details of his visit.
Seven people, including five Americans, were killed in a bombing at a U.S.-run military training centre in Riyadh in November 1995. Four Saudis were beheaded for carrying out the attack.

Another attack in June 1996 killed 19 American servicemen when a fuel truck blew up at a complex housing U.S. military personnel in the eastern Saudi city of Khobar. Saudi Arabia has yet to reveal the results of its investigation into the blast.
About 5,700 U.S. troops are stationed in the kingdom as part of coalition forces policing a no-fly zone over southern Iraq.
Shalikashvili arrived from Egypt on the second leg of a Middle East tour which is to include Israel. He is to return to the United States on Friday.
